in_text_mentions: Furuncles mainly affect areas rich in hair follicles, such as the armpits and the gluteal region, with the formation of abscesses in the hypodermis. Hair follicles are the gateway to S. aureus, favoring its development. It usually presents as an erythematous, painful, and floating nodule, with pustules on the surface and a drainage point. A single or multiple concomitant lesions can be observed (Fig. 10).Figure 10MRSA furunculosis. A healthy 42-year-old patient with several abscesses and furuncles. Positive culture for MRSA with production of Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a human patient explicitly captioned as a carbuncle in insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus. The image visibly shows the classic carbuncle phenotype: an infiltrated erythematous-wine colored plaque with a central ulcerated necrotic core/eschar and purulent drainage, matching the caption and the in-text definition of carbuncle as coalescent furuncles with multiple drainage sinus tracts. Fair/light surrounding skin is visible; no ethnicity or age is stated. No diagrams, controls, or other-disease panels present. [raw subtype: carbuncle]

in_text_mentions: The patient was admitted into the hospital and was treated with empirical antibiotic therapy: amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 1 g/200 mg IV + clindamycin 600 mg IV every 8 hours. panels.rationale: Real-patient clinical photograph of a solitary erythematous subcutaneous nodule with a central punctum on the posterior left thigh, showing the classic furuncular morphology of furuncle_carbuncle; the lesion is explicitly captioned as furuncle-like and the article is indexed under furuncle_carbuncle with prior triage 'keep'. The single lesion with a central punctum supports subtype furuncle (not carbuncle, which requires multiple draining openings), and no purulent drainage or necrotic core plug is described. Attribution confidence is tempered slightly because the punctum contains an extruding larva (furuncular myiasis presentation), but the visibly demonstrated manifestation is a furuncular nodule with central punctum. [raw subtype: furuncle]

in_text_mentions: On examination, she was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. A solitary subcutaneous lesion was present on the posterior left upper thigh, with a central punctum at the site of larval extrusion (Figure 1). There was minimal surrounding induration without fluctuance, extensive erythema, active drainage, or regional lymphadenopathy. The remainder of the examination was unremarkable.
